Where it began

Harshit Rana comes from Ghevra, close to where Delhi meets Haryana, and was born on 22 December 2001. He started training at ten. At Ganga International School his promise caught the eye of the coach Shravan Kumar, who gave him his first formal grounding in the game.

He came through with Delhi, and in February 2022 the Kolkata Knight Riders bought him at the Indian Premier League auction. His first Twenty20 match came for them on 28 April that year.

The player

Rana took his chance in the IPL. In the 2024 season he took 19 wickets in 13 matches at 20.16, joint-fourth among all the bowlers in the competition. His Test chance came on 22 November 2024, in the first match of the Border-Gavaskar Trophy against Australia at Perth, about as demanding a place to start as the game offers. By November 2026 he had played two Tests and taken four wickets at 50.75, with a best of 3 for 48.

One-day cricket brought quicker rewards. He took 3 for 53 on his debut against England in February 2025, and was part of the India squads that won the Champions Trophy and the Asia Cup that year. In October 2025 his 4 for 39 in Sydney were the best figures an Indian bowler had taken at the SCG.

Handy with the bat

He can bat, too. In the 2023 Duleep Trophy quarter-final, playing for North Zone, he hit 122 not out from 86 balls for his first first-class hundred.

New Zealand saw both sides of his game in January 2026. At Vadodara he removed both their openers, Devon Conway and Henry Nicholls, and then made a quick 29 from 23 balls to help India over the line. In the third match he took three more wickets and hit 52 from 43 balls, his first one-day fifty, with four sixes along the way, sharing a big stand with Virat Kohli. His Test batting had been quieter, with seven runs from three innings by November 2026. Given what he had done elsewhere, that looked like a figure with room to grow.

And finally

His first caps in the three international formats came in quick succession. His Test debut came in November 2024. His first T20 International followed against England at Pune on 31 January 2025, and he arrived in it partway through the match, coming on as a replacement for Shivam Dube. Six days later he was making his one-day debut against the same opponents. For a young man from Ghevra, it was a busy winter.
